kept.title: Arbitrary Command Injection in Benchmarking Utility
kept.description: The `exec` function in `benchmarking/compare/index.js` constructs shell commands using unvalidated user-provided input from `process.argv`.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a branch argument containing shell metacharacters, e.g., 'main; rm -rf /'.
Pass the malicious string to `pnpm bench:compare <malicious_input>`.
The `checkout` function executes the unsanitized input via `execSync`.
kept.impact: Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the developer machine or CI environment running the benchmarks.

kept.title: Insecure Use of --allow-natives-syntax in Benchmarks
kept.description: The benchmark scripts are run with `--allow-natives-syntax`, which exposes V8 internal functions like `%CollectGarbage`, increasing the attack surface for potential V8 exploits.
steps_to_exploit: Access the benchmarking environment where this flag is enabled.
Inject a payload utilizing V8-specific natives to perform out-of-bounds access or memory corruption.
Execute the script via `pnpm bench`.
kept.impact: Exploitation of the JavaScript engine, potentially leading to privilege escalation or sandbox escapes.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution through Unsafe Object Reconstruction
kept.description: The `unflatten` function in `src/parse.js` lacks comprehensive checks against '__proto__' or other prototype-modifying keys when building objects, potentially enabling prototype pollution.
steps_to_exploit: Prepare a malicious JSON payload with a key set to '__proto__'.
Pass the payload to `devalue.parse()`.
The parser manually assigns keys to objects without fully sanitizing the target key name, potentially modifying `Object.prototype`.
kept.impact: Prototype pollution can lead to Denial of Service or downstream XSS/RCE depending on how the application handles objects.

kept.title: Deserialization of untrusted input causing memory exhaustion
kept.description: The parser uses `new Array(length)` based on the `length` property found in the serialized input, which can be manipulated to cause massive memory allocation (DoS).
steps_to_exploit: Craft a serialized payload indicating an extremely large array length (e.g., 2^32 - 1).
Call `devalue.parse()` on the payload.
The engine attempts to allocate a massive amount of memory for the array.
kept.impact: Application process crash due to Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors, causing a Denial of Service.

kept.title: Lack of Input Validation on Parsed Values
kept.description: The parser relies heavily on the structure of the input array without sufficient validation of indices or types within nested structures.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a specially crafted array index that points to an invalid structure.
The logic fails to properly validate the `index` before accessing `values[index]`.
This could lead to type confusion during hydration.
kept.impact: Unexpected application state, crashes, or potential logic vulnerabilities.

kept.title: Exposure of Internals in benchmarking/compare/runner.js
kept.description: The runner uses `process.send` to pass results, but it does not validate the structure or contents of the results retrieved from the benchmarks.
steps_to_exploit: Modify a benchmark file to return malicious data structures that override system objects.
Run the compare tool.
The main process deserializes and processes the malicious output.
kept.impact: Information disclosure or malicious code execution within the runner context.

kept.title: Potential Integer Overflow in Array Indexing
kept.description: The code uses bitwise operations or simple addition to handle array lengths and indices, which may overflow if inputs are not properly checked against JS safe integer limits.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a large numerical input for array lengths/indices.
The system uses `2 ** 32 - 1` as `MAX_ARRAY_LEN` but fails to check for overflows during arithmetic operations inside `hydrate`.
kept.impact: Incorrect data retrieval or memory management errors.

kept.title: Insecure Temporal object construction
kept.description: The `fromStringValue` method dynamically calls `Temporal[tag.slice(9)].from(text)`, which is highly risky if the tag string is not strictly validated.
steps_to_exploit: Supply a crafted string with a tag that allows access to unintended properties of the global Temporal object.
The code dynamically accesses a method based on the string.
kept.impact: Unintended function execution or potential information leakage.

kept.title: Unsafe buffer creation in base64.js legacy path
kept.description: The legacy `decode_legacy` function performs a character-by-character conversion, which can be inefficient and susceptible to memory exhaustion if extremely large strings are processed.
steps_to_exploit: Send an enormous Base64 encoded string.
The loop iterates over the length of the string, allocating a Uint8Array proportional to the input.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via memory exhaustion.

kept.title: Missing validation of `byteOffset` and `length` in View creation
kept.description: The `fromViewInfo` method trusts the `byteOffset` and `length` values provided by the serialized input when calling the TypedArray constructor.
steps_to_exploit: Construct a malformed payload where the `byteOffset` plus `length` exceeds the size of the underlying buffer.
The TypedArray constructor will throw a range error, which might be caught or handled improperly in the parent routine.
kept.impact: Denial of Service through unhandled exceptions.

kept.title: Circular reference handling in custom revivers
kept.description: The hydration logic for custom revivers attempts to detect circular dependencies with a `Set`, but this could be bypassed if the user reviver is malicious.
steps_to_exploit: Create a custom reviver that initiates its own recursion.
The check `hydrating.has(i)` may not cover all complex circular dependency scenarios, potentially leading to stack overflow.
kept.impact: Denial of Service via infinite recursion (Stack Overflow).

kept.title: Insecure use of String.fromCharCode.apply
kept.description: Using `String.fromCharCode.apply` with large chunks can lead to stack overflow on older engines or with large data sizes.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a very large array to `encode_legacy`.
The `apply` call with a large array of arguments will exceed the call stack size.
kept.impact: Denial of Service via stack overflow.

kept.title: Reliance on `globalThis` for constructor lookup
kept.description: The `fromViewInfo` operation performs a dynamic lookup on `globalThis` using an unvalidated tag string.
steps_to_exploit: Supply a tag that refers to an unintended global constructor (e.g., 'Function').
The parser might attempt to construct a dangerous object.

kept.title: Insecure performance tracking
kept.description: The performance tracker uses `setTimeout(f, 10)` which, if run in a high-frequency loop, can cause significant event loop lag.
steps_to_exploit: Run the benchmark tool repeatedly or in an environment where resource exhaustion is prioritized.
The event loop is blocked by numerous small timeouts.
kept.impact: Denial of Service by starving the Node.js event loop.

kept.title: Unbounded output from benchmark stringify results
kept.description: The benchmark output formatting logic `console.log` doesn't limit the output size, allowing massive JSON objects to be printed to the console.
steps_to_exploit: Generate massive results from a benchmark run.
The `fs.writeFileSync` or `console.log` call will attempt to buffer the entire large string.
kept.impact: Memory consumption increase, leading to system degradation or DoS.
